name: @gjsify/gtk-runtime-win32-x64
description: Batteries-included GTK/GObject-Introspection runtime bundle for Windows x64 — lets @gjsify/node-gi load gi:// namespaces (GLib/GObject/Gio/cairo/Pango/Graphene/Gdk) with NO gvsbuild/system GTK. Platform-gated (win32/x64 only).

gaps.why: gvsbuild carries gst-plugins-good's mpg123 element only if libmpg123 was built, and it was not. Measured on the published 0.47.0 and unchanged on 0.48.0: a bundled mp3 fails as "missing a plug-in" and an mp3 stream as "Internal data stream error", which reads like a missing TLS backend and is not (#1544, #1626).

`ogg` ships and demuxes the container, and nothing decodes the Vorbis stream inside it. Same upstream cause as MP3 — the gst-plugins-base element links libvorbis, which this gvsbuild prefix did not build (#1626).
the gst-plugins-good element links libFLAC, absent from this gvsbuild prefix for the same reason as the two above (#1626).

the modern Windows sink, and the one absence here that costs no format: `directsound` ships and `autoaudiosink` resolves to it. Declared because it is the same silent absence, not because anything breaks.

`isomp4` demuxes the container and `audioparsers` supplies `aacparse`, after which the stream reaches no decoder at all. The two elements that would decode it are `faad` (gst-plugins-bad, GPL) and `avdec_aac` (libav, whose whole closure these bundles refuse), so shipping one is a redistribution decision for whoever ships the product rather than this bundle's.
